title: 04. OOP: 01 — Object Oriented Programming in Python (Complete Deep Dive)
summary: Goal: After reading this, no OOP question — basic, tricky, or rare — should surprise you.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
> **Goal**: After reading this, no OOP question — basic, tricky, or rare — should surprise you.

OOP = modeling real-world things as **objects** that bundle **data (attributes)** and **behavior (methods)**. In Python, _everything_ is an object — even functions, classes, modules, and types themselves.

sections.title: 1. The four pillars (with exact definitions)
sections.body:
| Pillar            | One-line meaning                       | Hides what?    | Example                   |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Encapsulation** | Bundle data + methods + control access | internal state | `__balance` in `Account`  |
| **Abstraction**   | Expose _what_, hide _how_              | implementation | `ABC`, interfaces         |
| **Inheritance**   | Reuse and extend another class         | repetition     | `Dog(Animal)`             |
| **Polymorphism**  | Same call works on different types     | type details   | `len(x)` on str/list/dict |

Memorize: _Encapsulation hides data, Abstraction hides implementation, Inheritance reuses, Polymorphism replaces._

sections.title: 2. Class & Object — internals
sections.body:
### 2.1 Anatomy

```python
class Car:
    """Docstring."""

    wheels = 4                     # CLASS attribute (shared, lives on class)
    _registry = []                 # also class-level

    def __init__(self, brand):     # initializer (instance method)
        self.brand = brand         # INSTANCE attribute (per object)
        Car._registry.append(self)

    def drive(self):
        return f"{self.brand} driving"

    @classmethod
    def count(cls):                # bound to the class
        return len(cls._registry)

    @staticmethod
    def is_valid_brand(b):         # plain function namespaced under class
        return isinstance(b, str) and b
```

### 2.2 What `self` actually is

- The first argument the bound method receives.
- Convention only — `def drive(this)` works.
- A **bound method** = function + instance pre-bound:
  ```python
  c.drive          # <bound method Car.drive of <Car ...>>
  Car.drive(c)     # equivalent to c.drive()
  ```

### 2.3 Class vs Instance attributes — the trap

```python
class A:
    items = []                       # SHARED!
a, b = A(), A()
a.items.append(1)
print(b.items)                       # [1] surprise
```

Fix: initialize mutables in `__init__`:

```python
def __init__(self): self.items = []
```

### 2.4 Attribute lookup order (very common interview)

For `obj.x`:

1. **Data descriptors** on the type (`@property`)
2. **Instance `__dict__`**
3. **Class attributes / non-data descriptors** along **MRO**
4. `__getattr__` (only if 1–3 failed)

This is why `@property` overrides instance attributes but a plain class attribute does not.

sections.title: 3. Encapsulation — exhaustive
sections.body:
### 3.1 Three visibility levels (by convention)

| Naming   | Meaning                        | Enforced?        |
| -------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| `name`   | public                         | –                |
| `_name`  | "internal use, may change"     | – (linters warn) |
| `__name` | name-mangled to `_Class__name` | partially        |

Name mangling avoids subclass clashes, not access. `obj._Class__name` still works.

### 3.2 Property — proper getter/setter

```python
class Temp:
    def __init__(self, c): self._c = c

    @property
    def celsius(self): return self._c

    @celsius.setter
    def celsius(self, v):
        if v < -273.15: raise ValueError
        self._c = v

    @celsius.deleter
    def celsius(self): del self._c

    @property
    def fahrenheit(self):                   # computed, read-only
        return self._c * 9/5 + 32
```

Looks like an attribute (`t.celsius = 25`) but runs your code. Add validation later without breaking callers.

### 3.3 `@cached_property` (3.8+)

Computes once, stores on instance, reads thereafter. Invalidate via `del obj.total`.

```python
from functools import cached_property
class Report:
    @cached_property
    def total(self): return expensive_sum(self.rows)
```

sections.title: 4. Abstraction — exhaustive
sections.body:
### 4.1 Abstract Base Classes (ABC)

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
class Payment(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def pay(self, amount): ...
    def receipt(self): return f"Paid via {type(self).__name__}"

class UPI(Payment):
    def pay(self, amount): print("UPI", amount)

# Payment()  → TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class
```

Abstract properties / classmethods supported:

```python
class Shape(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def area(self): ...
```

### 4.2 `Protocol` (PEP 544) — structural duck typing

```python
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
@runtime_checkable
class SupportsClose(Protocol):
    def close(self) -> None: ...

def shutdown(x: SupportsClose): x.close()
```

- ABC = nominal (must inherit). Protocol = structural (just needs the methods).
- Use Protocol for third-party types you cannot modify.

### 4.3 ABC vs Protocol

| Feature                  | ABC               | Protocol                       |
| ------------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Subclass must inherit    | Yes               | No                             |
| Runtime enforcement      | Yes               | Only with `@runtime_checkable` |
| Concrete methods allowed | Yes               | Yes (default impls)            |
| Best for                 | Libraries you own | External / duck-typed          |

sections.title: 5. Inheritance — exhaustive
sections.body:
### 5.1 Types

- **Single**: `class B(A)`
- **Multilevel**: `A → B → C`
- **Hierarchical**: many children of one parent
- **Multiple**: `class C(A, B)`
- **Hybrid**: combination
- **Diamond**: solved by MRO

### 5.2 `super()` — what it really does

- Returns a proxy delegating to the **next class in MRO**, not the literal parent.
- Each class calls `super().__init__()` once; diamond's top runs once.

```python
class A:
    def __init__(self): print("A")
class B(A):
    def __init__(self): super().__init__(); print("B")
class C(A):
    def __init__(self): super().__init__(); print("C")
class D(B, C):
    def __init__(self): super().__init__(); print("D")
D()    # A C B D    ← MRO: D B C A
```

### 5.3 MRO & C3 Linearization

- `print(D.__mro__)` or `D.mro()`.
- Rules: child before parents, base order preserved, each class once.
- If C3 can't merge → `TypeError: Cannot create a consistent MRO`.

### 5.4 Liskov violation (concrete bug)

```python
class Bird:
    def fly(self): ...
class Penguin(Bird):
    def fly(self): raise NotImplementedError
```

Code expecting any `Bird` to fly breaks. Fix: split — `Bird`, `FlyingBird(Bird)`, `Penguin(Bird)`.

### 5.5 Composition — when NOT to inherit

```python
class Engine: ...
class Car:
    def __init__(self): self.engine = Engine()
```

Easier tests, no MRO surprises, no fragile base class.

### 5.6 Aggregation vs Composition (UML)

- **Composition**: child created and owned by parent (lifetime tied).
- **Aggregation**: child passed in, outlives parent.

sections.title: 6. Polymorphism — exhaustive
sections.body:
### 6.1 Forms

1. **Ad-hoc / overloading** — Python keeps last `def`. Simulate via:
   - default args, `*args/**kwargs` + branching
   - `functools.singledispatch` (single-arg type)
   - `multipledispatch` (3rd party) for multi-arg
2. **Subtype / overriding** — subclass redefines.
3. **Parametric / generics** — `list[int]`, `Generic[T]`.
4. **Duck typing** — Python's default; cares about behavior, not type.

### 6.2 `singledispatch`

```python
from functools import singledispatch
@singledispatch
def to_json(x): raise TypeError(type(x))
@to_json.register
def _(x: int): return str(x)
@to_json.register
def _(x: list): return "[" + ",".join(to_json(i) for i in x) + "]"
```

### 6.3 Operator overloading

`a + b` → `a.__add__(b)`; if `NotImplemented`, tries `b.__radd__(a)`. (See file 17.)

### 6.4 Override decorator (3.12+)

```python
from typing import override
class Dog(Animal):
    @override
    def speak(self): print("woof")
```

Helps type-checker catch typos that miss the override.

sections.title: 7. Method types — full picture
8. Descriptors — the hidden engine
sections.body:
### 8.1 What is a descriptor?

Any object defining `__get__`, `__set__`, or `__delete__`. They control attribute access on the _class_ level.

- **Data descriptor**: has `__set__`/`__delete__` → wins over instance dict.
- **Non-data descriptor**: only `__get__` → loses to instance dict.

`property`, `classmethod`, `staticmethod`, ORM fields — all descriptors.

### 8.2 Validating descriptor

```python
class Positive:
    def __set_name__(self, owner, name):
        self.private = f"_{name}"
    def __get__(self, obj, owner=None):
        if obj is None: return self
        return getattr(obj, self.private)
    def __set__(self, obj, value):
        if value < 0: raise ValueError
        setattr(obj, self.private, value)

class Account:
    balance = Positive()
    def __init__(self, b): self.balance = b
```

This is how mini-ORMs (SQLAlchemy, Django) build their fields.

sections.title: 9. __slots__ — memory & speed
sections.body:
```python
class Point:
    __slots__ = ("x", "y")
```

- Removes per-instance `__dict__` and `__weakref__`.
- Saves ~50% memory; faster attribute access.
- No dynamic attributes, harder multiple inheritance, no monkey-patching.
- Dataclass equivalent: `@dataclass(slots=True)` (3.10+).

sections.title: 10. Metaclasses — the type of types
sections.body:
```python
class Meta(type):
    def __new__(mcs, name, bases, ns):
        ns["created_by"] = "Meta"
        return super().__new__(mcs, name, bases, ns)

class A(metaclass=Meta): ...
print(A.created_by)        # Meta
```

- A class is itself an instance of its metaclass. `type` is the default.
- Used by frameworks (Django Model, SQLAlchemy declarative, ABC, Enum).
- 99% of code should use `__init_subclass__` instead.

### 10.1 `__init_subclass__` (lighter alternative)

```python
class Plugin:
    registry = []
    def __init_subclass__(cls, **kw):
        super().__init_subclass__(**kw)
        Plugin.registry.append(cls)
```

13. Magic methods you must override (subset)
sections.body:
(Full list in [17_magic_methods.md](17_magic_methods.md).)

- `__init__`, `__new__`, `__del__`
- `__repr__`, `__str__`, `__format__`
- `__eq__`, `__hash__`, `__lt__` (+ `functools.total_ordering`)
- `__len__`, `__bool__`
- `__iter__`, `__next__`, `__contains__`
- `__getitem__`, `__setitem__`, `__delitem__`
- `__call__`
- `__enter__`, `__exit__`
- `__copy__`, `__deepcopy__`

If you override `__eq__`, set `__hash__ = None` for mutable types or implement `__hash__` consistent with `__eq__`.

sections.title: 14. SOLID applied to OOP (preview)
sections.body:
- **S**ingle Responsibility: one class = one reason to change.
- **O**pen/Closed: extend by subclass/composition; don't edit closed code.
- **L**iskov: subtypes must be drop-in replacements.
- **I**nterface Segregation: many small interfaces over one fat one.
- **D**ependency Inversion: depend on abstractions; inject dependencies.

(Full discussion: [04_design_principles.md](04_design_principles.md).)

sections.title: 15. Common OOP design patterns
sections.body:
| Pattern         | One-liner                  | Pythonic shortcut            |
| --------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Singleton       | one instance               | module-level object          |
| Factory         | choose subclass            | function or `classmethod`    |
| Builder         | step-wise construction     | dataclass + chained methods  |
| Adapter         | wrap to new interface      | a class with the new methods |
| Decorator       | add behavior               | `@decorator`                 |
| Strategy        | pluggable algorithm        | pass a function              |
| Observer        | pub/sub                    | callbacks list               |
| Template Method | skeleton + hooks           | base with abstract steps     |
| State           | swap behavior with state   | dict of state classes        |
| Command         | encapsulate request        | callable object              |
| Iterator        | sequential traversal       | `__iter__` / generator       |
| Composite       | tree treated as leaf       | recursive class              |
| Proxy           | lazy / acl wrapper         | wrapper class                |
| Facade          | simple front, complex back | helper module                |

sections.title: 16. Class-related dunder cheat list
sections.body:
| Need                 | Method                                                              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Subclass hook        | `__init_subclass__`                                                 |
| Lazy attribute       | `@cached_property`                                                  |
| Custom attr access   | `__getattr__`, `__getattribute__`, `__setattr__`                    |
| Custom equality      | `__eq__` + `__hash__`                                               |
| Dict-like            | `__getitem__`, `__setitem__`, `__contains__`, `__iter__`, `__len__` |
| Generic subscription | `__class_getitem__`                                                 |

sections.title: 17. Performance & correctness gotchas
sections.body:
- Don't use mutable default args.
- Beware shared class-level mutables.
- `super()` no-arg form needs Python 3 _and_ class context.
- Don't override `__del__` casually — complicates GC of cycles.
- `@property` adds a function call per read — avoid in tight loops.
- Implementing `__eq__` without `__hash__` makes instances unhashable.
- `__slots__` doesn't compose with regular base classes silently — read the docs.
- `isinstance(x, ABC)` with `@runtime_checkable` Protocol can be slow; cache.

sections.title: 18. Quick reference patterns
sections.body:
### 18.1 Singleton (Pythonic — just use a module)

```python
# config.py
DEBUG = True
def reload(): ...
```

`import config`. Done.

### 18.2 Factory

```python
def make(kind): return {"a": A, "b": B}[kind]()
```

### 18.3 Strategy

```python
def sort_by(strategy, items): return strategy(items)
sort_by(sorted, data)
```

### 18.4 Observer

```python
class Subject:
    def __init__(self): self._obs = []
    def attach(self, fn): self._obs.append(fn)
    def notify(self, ev):
        for fn in self._obs: fn(ev)
```
